result.name: auth_rls_initplan
result.title: Auth RLS Initialization Plan
result.description: Detects if calls to `current_setting()` and `auth.<function>()` in RLS policies are being unnecessarily re-evaluated for each row
result.detail: Table `public.projects` has a row level security policy `fixture_project_access` that re-evaluates current_setting() or auth.<function>() for each row. This produces suboptimal query performance at scale. Resolve the issue by replacing `auth.<function>()` with `(select auth.<function>())`. See [docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security#call-functions-with-select) for more info.

native.compatibilityNote: Native peer sample precedes a compatibility-only queue terminal-reason correction. Final SQL metadata is independently regenerated and parsed by the real connection-settings Core decoder; adoption body/receipt policy and counter semantics are unchanged.

Tapping actual switch turns consent on and enables Review
Reviewed queue count is exposed as one labelled accessible element with value 2
Explicit pause body is persisted/sent once, confirmation succeeds and normal workspace refresh completes with empty local queue
Default light iPhone/iPad screenshots reviewed for readable action counts
limits: No new installed Mac, physical device, large text/dark/contrast, keyboard or spoken VoiceOver acceptance
No installed OS relaunch acceptance specific to the new count fields; exact lost-reply/relaunch codec/model behavior is covered in Core and earlier OS adoption recovery remains separate evidence

scope: Optional connection_policy=pause is an explicit consent field; unselected/legacy clients remain blocked for affected bindings/retained queue
Policy-aware immutable review uses a v2 HMAC proof binding the action and exact five counts, while no-policy proof and applied old receipt recovery stay compatible

Atomic commit keeps personal email and verified project hooks paused, cancels unverified project setups, retires only affected queued payloads and preserves unrelated/global settings and other queued work
File custody and live write permits still refuse the entire transfer without partial pause; late custody faults roll back all private state/epochs/queue counters
Receipts and private device-only retry journal retain policy plus bounded numeric effects, with strict decode/misroute/counter validation and no names/addresses/endpoints/credentials/task text
Native review defaults consent off, explains all effects, exposes labelled count values and includes saved-request actions on recovery
Existing resource_unavailable delivery status preserves old edge/client validators; actual SQL webhook receipt parses in connection settings
limits: No credential/address/endpoint retarget into a team; supported destination reauthorization remains open
Personal email/webhook settings still need team-destination filtering, disabled Resume/verification and clear explanations for adopted projects; server already rejects unsupported personal writes
A separate persistent pause/preparation flow before draining a busy wire permit is not implemented; the current atomic action refuses all changes while sends remain live
File/provider custody, native stage scroll/focus polish, remaining Mac/account/window/accessibility/load and hosted/provider acceptance remain open

No real user data, system settings, hosted schema/configuration or ordinary feature rollout changed; all user-deferred release/signing/distribution, general older-client rollout, remote reminders, OAuth/provider/domain setup and physical location work remain deferred
Adoption, rank 6 and the wider remaining Px plan are not complete
diagnostics: Initial SQL assertion compared the receipt against a superseded pre-file-test queue count. Fresh review correctly included later queued events; the test now binds the final 12-event review.
Native DTO pause-blocker validation was updated to account for the explicit policy while retaining strict file and count checks.

UIKit exposes a switch-sized action inside a label-sized accessibility frame; the test now taps the observed switch control and verifies value 1. The app correctly kept Review disabled when consent remained off.
Each count is now one explicitly labelled/value-bearing accessibility element; tests inspect its display frame and value rather than requiring noninteractive text to be tappable.
iPad scroll helper stops at the visible header instead of over-scrolling and dismissing the sheet. Earlier diagnostic failures are not reported as passing runs.
Cross-component review caught an unrecognized new queue status; the final implementation reuses resource_unavailable and tests the SQL-generated webhook receipt through the existing decoder.
